about.title: Thousand Oaks Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Thousand Oaks sits along the US-101 Ventura Freeway, and much of the city's traffic funnels on and off it through Thousand Oaks Boulevard, Moorpark Road and Hillcrest Drive. Those four corridors show up most often in public collision records here. In 2025, the last complete reporting year, Thousand Oaks logged 616 injury collisions, with 859 people hurt and 4 lives lost. Crash reports cluster on Tuesday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when commuters head home. If one of those numbers now describes your week, the paperwork can feel heavier than the injuries. LawProactive exists to take one task off your plate. Tell us what happened, and at no cost we connect you with an independent Ventura County attorney who handles car accident claims on contingency. You pay nothing unless your case recovers money. From there, the attorney can deal with adjusters, gather the police report and camera footage, and keep track of California's two-year filing deadline while you focus on getting better.

whyChoose.title: Why Thousand Oaks Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines That Are Easy to Miss
items.desc: California gives you two years to file a car accident lawsuit, but a claim involving a city, county or Caltrans vehicle can require notice in as little as six months. Getting connected early means those dates are calendared before they become a problem.

items.title: Your Share of Fault Is Not the End of the Story
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if an adjuster argues you were partly to blame; your award is reduced by your percentage, not erased. An attorney can push back when the other side inflates that percentage.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering, No Fee Up Front
items.desc: California does not limit non-economic damages in ordinary car accident cases, so your pain, sleeplessness and lost time count. The attorneys we connect you with work on contingency, so there is no bill unless your case recovers money.

items.question: The other driver's insurer wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to another driver's insurance company, and it is usually wiser not to. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to shift blame or minimize your injuries. Politely decline, save any messages they send you, and let an attorney handle those conversations.

items.question: I was hit on the 101 in Thousand Oaks but live in another county. Does that matter?
items.answer: Not much for your claim itself. A crash on the Ventura Freeway in Thousand Oaks is generally handled under Ventura County jurisdiction, and the CHP or Thousand Oaks police report will be the starting record. An attorney in our network can request that report and any nearby camera footage for you, wherever you live.

items.question: What should I be saving right now?
items.answer: Keep photos of every vehicle, the roadway and your injuries, along with the names of anyone who stopped to help. Hold onto medical bills, repair estimates and pay stubs showing missed work. Do not repair or sell your car until the damage has been documented, and avoid posting about the crash on social media.
